simple.meaning: גָּדֵל (gâdêl) is a Hebrew action word meaning “large (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Genesis, 1 Samuel, 2 Chronicles, Ezekiel, beginning at Genesis 26:13. The surrounding contexts include Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּדֵל (H1432) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גָּדֵל (gâdêl) / H1432 is traced through Genesis 26:13, 1 Samuel 2:26, 2 Chronicles 17:12, Ezekiel 16:26 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1432. gadel גָּדֵל participle masculine or verbal adjective becoming great, growing up , Gen 26:13 (J) 1Sam 2:26 (compare Dr) 2Chr 17:12 ; also great, plural construct בָשָׂר גִּדִלֵי Ezek 16:26 great of flesh.

occurrences.englishText: The man grew great, and grew more and more until he became very great.
The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Yahweh and also with men.
Jehoshaphat grew great exceedingly; and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah.
You have also committed sexual immorality with the Egyptians, your neighbors, great of flesh; and have multiplied your prostitution, to provoke me to anger.
